episode_row: confirmation counter logged "0 new" while lineups flipped the pick

commits.subject: fix(scheduler): track lineup confirmations at team level, not game level
commits.body:
Bug: count_new_confirmations reported 0 new confirmations when a game
had previously been partially confirmed (e.g., only the home team's
lineup posted) and then the away team posted its lineup. The game was
already in the tracking set, so no new game → 0. But the prediction
pipeline uses per-side lineup data, so the newly posted side DID
change the inputs — the log message just hid it.

Observed live on 2026-04-12: two back-to-back lineup-check runs,
both against the same 14-game confirmed set. Run 1 saw "6 teams
using projected lineups" and picked Roman Anthony. Run 2 reported
"0 new confirmed lineup(s)" yet the prediction dropped to "3 teams
projected" and flipped the pick to Brendan Donovan. The 3 additional
team-level confirmations were real; the old game-level counter just
couldn't see them.

Fix: `check_confirmed_lineups` now returns `dict[int, set[str]]`
(game_pk → set of confirmed sides). `count_new_confirmations` tracks
a `set[tuple[int, str]]` of (game_pk, side) pairs and counts each
newly confirmed side separately. run_day passes this set instead of
a set of game_pks; `state.confirmed_game_pks` is now derived from
the side set for backward compatibility of the scheduler_state.json
schema. DH game 2 recheck uses the same tuple set.

Test updates:
  - check_confirmed_lineups return type changed from bool → set[str]
    in existing tests
  - counts_new_confirmations: a fully confirmed game now counts as 2
    (both sides), not 1
  - New regression test: game with (pk, "away") already in the set
    gets the (pk, "home") side confirmed → counts as +1, not 0
